analysis:
This PR changes only scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, a CI test harness with no runtime provider or coordinator code. The diff adds a HOURLY constant (head lines 134-136), includes ci-dev-hourly.yml in the workflow-classification test (lines 709-710), and adds test_hourly_full_run_only_dispatches_ci_dev_on_dev (lines 954-972). That test pins the hourly workflow: schedule and workflow_dispatch triggers only, cron '7 * * * *', top-level `permissions: {}`, a single ubuntu-24.04 job with exactly {actions: write, contents: read}, no `uses:`, secrets, checkout, id-token, self-hosted or darkbloom- labels, and exactly one `gh workflow run ci-dev.yml --ref dev`. These are tightening assertions that constrain the new workflow, and I see no weakening of existing checks. The existing tests (unchanged context) keep release and credentialed workflows on literal Blacksmith runners and keep routed jobs read-only with no id-token or secrets.

The new workflow file ci-dev-hourly.yml is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that it actually meets the pinned constraints. Specifically, I could not confirm that the `actions: write` token cannot be misused, or that the schedule runs only on the default branch. Those tests would catch regressions in CI, but the workflow's real content needs review in whichever batch contains it. No threat-model assets (A-001 to A-020) or boundaries (TB-002 to TB-014) are touched by this test-only change. The cache threat T-041 context is irrelevant here.
